title: Risk‑Tiered Pricing + Onboarding Credit Experiment with Automated Questionnaire Validation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: Enterprise procurement cycles are a large source of friction for Dedicated and Private deals. We frequently see procurement delaying signings due to SOC2 evidence collection, insurance verification, and bespoke contract SLAs. This experiment tests a combined product + pricing approach: create a risk‑tiered pricing ladder that grants onboarding credits (via invoice credit or committed capacity offset) when vendors complete an automated questionnaire and provide verifiable SOC2/insurance evidence through our vendor portal. Goals: 1) Reduce time-to-contract for mid-market and enterprise customers by 25% for cases where automated validation succeeds. 2) Increase conversion from RFQ to paid commit by 10% for pilot accounts. 3) Validate operational overhead and fraud vector risk introduced by automated evidence checks. Scope: - Build a questionnaire validation flow in the vendor portal that can accept uploaded SOC2 artifacts, cert URLs, and insurance binder PDFs. - Implement a rules engine to assign risk tiers (Low/Medium/High) based on answers and verified artifacts. - Offer onboarding credit amounts mapped to risk tier and commitment level (e.g., Low = $10k credit on annual Dedicated commit). - Add UI in the console onboarding flow to display credit eligibility and next steps. - Instrument metrics: time from first contact to signed contract, percent of vendors qualifying for Low risk tier, abuse incidents flagged, manual review rate, and credit utilization. Out of scope: - Full legal redesign of contract templates (we will use existing templates with addendum for credits). - Replacing SOC2 attestation manual review entirely; manual review remains fallback for borderline cases. Success metrics: - 25% reduction in procurement lead time for qualifying vendors. - >= 10 qualifying vendors in pilot within first 6 weeks. - Manual review rate <= 30% of submissions. - No material increase in fraud incidents (operational risk assessment to flag any >5% increase). Acceptance criteria: - Vendor portal accepts uploads and validates file metadata (hash and metadata). - Rules engine returns a deterministic tier and recommended credit within 500ms per submission. - Backend exposes audit log entries for each validation step (for legal and security review). - Finance and Legal sign-off on credit playbook and stop-loss thresholds. Rollout plan: 1) Alpha: internal sales+SE funnel (2 pilot customers) — 2 weeks. 2) Beta: invite-only mid-market cohort via growth team — 4 weeks. 3) Public pilot: opt-in for new Dedicated/Private trial signups — 6 weeks with monitoring and kill-switch. Success gating: finance approval on credit accounting, security sign-off on evidence storage, and legal approval on addendum. KPIs & dashboards: - Contract conversion funnel (lead -> proposal -> signed) annotated with onboarding credit flag. - Portal validation times and manual review queue depth. - Credit burn rate and impact on ARR. Key stakeholders: PM (Aisha Kumar), Engineering lead (Daniel Park), Security (Lena Fischer), Legal (Maya Thompson), Finance (Omar Reyes), Sales pilot owners (Sarah Ng). Risks & mitigations: - Fraudulent uploads: implement file metadata checks and sample manual reviews; set conservative credit caps for first 90 days. - Finance exposure: use committed capacity offset versus cash credit where possible to limit cash flow risk. - Legal/regulatory: require minimum contract language and holdback clause for credit clawback. Open questions: - Exact credit mapping by tier and commit size (finance to provide rate card). - Which insurance binder fields are sufficient for automation (security/legal to confirm). - Data retention and audit retention window for uploaded artifacts.
